title: Female Mahogany Jerusalem Cricket Eaton LACO
author: Dr. David Weissman, California Academy of Sciences
changes: Real recording of a female mahogany Jerusalem cricket (Ammopelmatus) drumming her abdomen on the ground to attract a mate, used for the weta: no free recording of a weta exists, and Jerusalem crickets are close relatives of weta in the same insect superfamily (Stenopelmatoidea); some weta also drum this way. Trimmed to 15.75–18.45 s of the original, mixed to mono, gentle 12 dB/oct high-pass at 70 Hz, silence trimmed, loudness-normalised (≈ −18 dBFS RMS, peak ≤ −1 dBFS), 10 ms fade-in / 120 ms fade-out, encoded as 96 kbps mono MP3. Recording by Dr. David Weissman (California Academy of Sciences), provided by Dr. Amy Vandergast (U.S. Geological Survey). The 70 Hz high-pass removes measured low-frequency background rumble between the drum rolls.
